title: G2M compliance claim plays and audit-log language
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working G2M brief and claims playbook for Security & Compliance positioning across sales, marketing, and legal review. Audience: product marketing, sales enablement, legal, security, and customer success. Goal: provide safe, high-impact customer-facing language about SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, clear audit-log claims, and a short competitive note to help reps counter common objections.

Claim taxonomy (for reps and copywriters)
- Sales-safe (green): Short, truthful, approved by security. Can be used in public collateral and demos.
- Customer-detail (amber): Use in direct sales conversations and SOWs; requires on-call product/security SME or approved one-pager.
- Legal/contract (redline): Language that must be validated by Legal/Contracts before inclusion in agreements or formal proposals.

High-level positioning (1–2 lines)
- Elevator pitch (sales-safe): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform built for production — with enterprise-grade controls, configurable private deployments, and comprehensive audit logs so teams can meet SOC2, ISO, and HIPAA requirements without building their own stack."
- Short website blurb (marketing): "Secure, observable inference — hosted, dedicated, or private deployments with SOC2-audited controls, ISO-aligned practices, and HIPAA support for regulated workloads."

Status snapshot (recommended phrasing for sales/marketing)
- SOC2 Type II: SOC2 Type II report covering Security and Availability controls — audited annually (Sales-safe).
- ISO/IEC 27001: Control framework aligned to ISO 27001 fundamentals; formal certification in progress (Customer-detail; target: Q3 2026).
- HIPAA: Support for PHI processing with a signed BAA; Private and Dedicated deployments are recommended for PHI (Sales-safe with caveats).
- Private deployments: VPC/on-prem options with KMS/HSM integrations for customer-managed keys (Sales-safe).

Suggested claim language by channel
- Website (public): "SOC2 Type II audited controls for Security & Availability. Private deployments and a signed BAA available for regulated data."
- Datasheet (customer-detail): "SOC2 Type II report (Security & Availability) available under NDA. ISO-aligned controls and a BAA template are available; Private/Dedicated deployment recommended for PHI. Audit logs capture request metadata, routing decisions, model_version, token usage, latency, and error codes; retention and redaction configurable per contract."
- Sales email snippet (short): "We maintain SOC2 Type II audited controls and offer a BAA for PHI — many customers run regulated workloads on Redwood Private. If you’d like, I can share our audit-log schema and a BAA sample."

Audit-log language (concrete, for datasheets and proposals)
- Sales-safe summary: "Structured audit logs for all inference requests, including timestamps, route, model_version, request_id, latency, token counts, routing/fallback events, and error codes. Logs are retained per contract and can be exported for customer audits."
- Customer-detail schema (for direct exchange, under NDA): "Fields typically logged: timestamp (UTC), customer_id, route_name, model_version, region, request_id, truncated_token_count, response_latency_ms, server_node_id, routing_policy, fallback_trigger_flag, error_code, outcome_summary. Input payload logging is optional and may be redacted or disabled; we recommend Private deployments for persistent PHI logging needs."
- Retention & redaction (legal note): "Default retention: 90 days. Enterprise add-on: configurable retention up to customer-defined periods; redaction and tokenization options available. Any claims about indefinite or >X year retention must be approved by Legal and Security."

Contract & BAA starter language (redline examples for Legal)
- BAA-friendly commitment (sales-safe until legal review): "Redwood will enter into a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for customers processing PHI. Private or Dedicated deployments are recommended for PHI use cases and will be subject to specific operational configurations set out in the BAA."
- Audit log clause (legal template snippet): "Provider will maintain structured audit logs sufficiently detailed to support customer audits of access and processing, including timestamps, request identifiers, and processing outcomes. Log retention, redaction, and export rights will be defined in the MSA/BAA."

Redlines and claims to avoid (don’t say these)
- Avoid absolute absolutes: "We never see customer data" — use "we do not use customer data to train models in hosted mode; technical measures are in place to prevent model training on customer inputs."
- Avoid conflating certifications: "ISO-certified SOC2" — incorrect. Say "SOC2 Type II audited controls" and separately state ISO alignment or certification progress.
- Avoid implying government-level accreditation unless we hold it.

Objection handling (short scripts)
- Customer: "How do you protect PHI in hosted mode?" Rep: "Hosted mode uses encryption at rest and in transit and has SOC2 controls; for PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with a signed BAA and customer-managed keys. I can connect you to our security team for architecture details."
- Customer: "Can we get a full SOC2 report?" Rep: "We can provide our SOC2 Type II report under NDA; I’ll raise a request with Security Ops and get you the export procedure."

Competitive positioning (notes for battlecards)
- Common opponent: Large single-tenant API provider (ManagedAPIX) — claim: ‘Fully managed with enterprise controls’. Counter: Redwood’s differentiator is the same control plane across Hosted, Dedicated, Private — customers can start hosted and move to private/dedicated without re-architecting their integration. Emphasize audit logs and key management parity across environments.
- Common opponent: Self-hosted open-source runtimes — claim: ‘Full control and no vendor risk’. Counter: Redwood offers on-prem/private deployments (BAA/KMS/HSM) plus production-grade serving runtime, kernel optimizations, and an observability stack (token-level cost/latency breakdowns) — lower operational lift and better SLOs.

Operational notes for CS/SEs (what to show in demos)
- Show audit-log viewer in Console: demonstrate fields (timestamp, request_id, model_version), search by request_id, export CSV.
- Demo KMS integration flow: rotate keys, show key IDs, and note how private deployments can lock keys to a customer HSM.
- Walkthrough BAA and SOC2 report request flow: expected SLA for report delivery and redaction steps.

Open items / next steps (owners assigned)
- Legal: finalize BAA template and audit-log contract language (owner: Miguel Santos, jira:SEC-1347).
- Security: publish an approved audit-log schema and retention tiers doc for GTM (owner: Jordan Wu).
- PMM: update website and datasheet copy once Legal approves final phrasing (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Sales Enablement: create a 1-pager cheat sheet and objection handling playbook (owner: Radhika Iyer).

Appendix: quick reference snippets (copy-paste)
- "SOC2 Type II audited controls for Security & Availability. Private deployments and BAAs available for regulated workloads."
- "Structured audit logs capturing timestamps, request_id, model_version, latency, routing decisions, and error codes. Retention and redaction configurable by contract."
- "We offer Private and Dedicated deployments with KMS/HSM integrations and optional customer-managed keys for stronger separation of duties."

Notes on tone and compliance discipline
- Keep public claims conservative and verifiable.
- Always append a CTA to connect customers to Security for deeper dives.
- When in doubt, route contractual or certification questions to Legal/Security before committing to timeframes or scope in public materials.

(End of draft)

Document history: initial draft 2025-11-12 by Aisha Patel. Reviewed 2026-01-09 by Security and 2026-02-20 by Legal. Pending final sign-off from Legal and PMM for website copy.
